title: Rework runtime artifact resolution to enable deterministic kernel selection
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Background: We have recurring nondeterministic kernel selection behavior across mixed-architecture fleets. Heuristics and lazy probing result in different kernel bundles chosen on cold-start vs warm-start which increases p50/p99 jitter and complicates rollouts for quantized model variants. This ticket refactors the artifact resolution path so the runtime chooses kernels deterministically based on a signed, versioned catalog produced during the build/packaging pipeline.

Scope:
- Introduce a build-time kernel catalog (catalog.json) that maps model fingerprint + quantization profile + hardware capability vector to an ordered list of compatible kernel bundles (cutlass/triton variants).
- Runtime will verify the catalog signature, load the precomputed ordering, and select the first compatible bundle using a deterministic compatibility check (no fuzzy heuristics).
- Add a lightweight in-memory resolution cache keyed by model-version+device-abi for fast subsequent selects.
- Telemetry: emit selection_reason and catalog_version in request traces and startup logs.
- Fallback: keep existing lazy probe fallback gated behind feature flag runtime.kern_select_v2 for controlled rollout.

Non-Goals:
- This ticket does not add new kernel implementations or change kernel internals.
- It does not change customer-facing API.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Deterministic selection observed in CI: repeated cold-starts of the same model on the same hardware choose the same kernel bundle in 100/100 runs.
- p50 and p99 cold-start variance reduction measurable in canary (baseline comparisons included).
- Signed catalog verification prevents runtime from trusting unsigned catalogs; runtime logs clear error and falls back to legacy probe when signature invalid.
- Feature flag rollout path exists and is documented.

Implementation Plan:
1) Catalog format design (schema + signing metadata). Deliverable: design doc + example catalog.
2) Build pipeline change: generate catalog during packaging and upload with artifacts. Deliverable: CI job modifications + artifact store layout.
3) Runtime changes: catalog verifier + deterministic selector + in-memory cache + telemetry hooks.
4) CI e2e: add repeated-start test harness and microbench for selection determinism.
5) Canary rollout: enable runtime.kern_select_v2 on a small GPU pool, observe telemetry and errors, then expand.

Testing Plan:
- Unit tests for catalog parsing, signature verification, and selection algorithm.
- Integration tests in the packaging pipeline to ensure catalogs accompany releases.
- Canary perf tests: compare 100-run cold-start kernel choices, and measure token latency variance on a representative quantized model (gpt-2-medium quantized path).

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Catalog generation misses a valid kernel variant, causing unnecessary fallback. Mitigation: include a catalog validation step that cross-checks available artifact inventory and flags mismatches at package time.
- Risk: Signature rollout may break older runtimes. Mitigation: catalog signature verification falls back to legacy mode if runtime capability not present; releases will include backward-compatible signed+unsigned catalogs for 2 releases.
- Risk: Larger catalog increases startup memory. Mitigation: compress catalog and only load subset for the present hardware profile; cache eviction for low-memory hosts.

Design Links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Deterministic+Kernel+Catalog (design doc), https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1KernCatalogArtifacts (example catalogs)

acceptance_criteria: 100/100 deterministic kernel selections in CI repeated-start test
catalog signature verification enforced when runtime supports it
telemetry emits selection_reason and catalog_version for every start
feature flag runtime.kern_select_v2 exists and can be toggled per-pool
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge behind flag and run internal CI for 1 week. Step 2: Canary on pool-3 (10 hosts) for 48h. Step 3: Expand to 20% of fleet, monitor catalog_miss_and_fallback and p99. Step 4: Full rollout if metrics stable for 72h.
implementation_notes:
- Keep legacy lazy-probe code path intact and gated.
- Add feature gate checks in startup path before catalog load.
- Use ed25519 signatures for catalogs; verify using embedded root public key or KMS-stored key.
- Ensure catalogs are monotonic; runtime rejects older catalog versions when set to 'strict' mode.
